claim: .github/workflows/gpu-burst-train.yml triggers on `issues: opened` (public repo, so any account that can open an issue can start the workflow run) and its job's sole gate is `contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'gpu-burst-train')` (line 63), with no actor-identity check anywhere in the file, unlike every other in-scope issues-triggered workflow that reads a sensitive secret.
evidence: grep -n "^on:\|types:\|^  issues:\|if:\|repository_owner\|user.login\|github.actor" .github/workflows/gpu-burst-train.yml -> `on: issues: types: [opened]` (lines 40-42), job `if: contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'gpu-burst-train')` (line 63), zero occurrences of `issue.user.login`, `repository_owner` or `github.actor ==` anywhere in the 217-line file. Cross-checked over the full 72-file scope with a Python/regex pass over every `on:` block + `secrets\.` reference: 28 files are `on: issues:`-triggered and read a secret other than GITHUB_TOKEN; 27 of 28 carry an `issue.user.login`/`repository_owner` guard, gpu-burst-train.yml is the sole exception. Job env: RUNPOD_API_KEY + VAST_API_KEY (Arm gate step, lines 119-138), RUNPOD_SSH_KEY added in the Burst step (140-153), VM_SSH_KEY in the 'Deliver + register bundle' step (173-217, SSH to the trainer VM), and checkout uses secrets.BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN (a PAT, line 257). Confirmed NOT currently exploited: `actions_list list_workflow_runs` for gpu-burst-train.yml, most recent 10 `event:issues` runs, all have `triggering_actor.login: benbaichmankass` and `conclusion: skipped`; `search_issues repo:benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights -author:benbaichmankass` returns 14 issues total, of which the only non-bot, non-owner author is `danleejames23` (issues #2680/#2681/#2688, all dated 2026-06-03, pre-dating the repo's 2026-07-07 'limit interactions to collaborators' setting per docs/security/intrusion-surface-audit-2026-06-28.md section 11) -- zero non-owner issues since. Could NOT verify the live 'Interaction limits' repository setting directly (no available tool reads it; same gap the 2026-06-28 audit itself flagged in its section 4 table).
expected: Per docs/security/intrusion-surface-audit-2026-06-28.md section 8 ('P1 -- Tier-1, fast-follow PR', item 3): 'Apply the identical author-guard to all remaining issues.opened-triggered privileged workflows ... (the SSH/SECRETS/token/provision set)', and section 11 (2026-07-07 addendum) states as verified fact: 'Every issue-triggered workflow (~30) gates on issue.user.login == github.repository_owner || github-actions[bot] -- a stranger can't fire a VM action even by opening a labelled issue.'
actual: gpu-burst-train.yml -- an SSH+SECRETS, issues-triggered, privileged workflow created after that 2026-07-07 addendum (its own header comments reference milestone M19 and provenance id PI-20260924-5V6UVR9J-0002, dating it to on or after 2026-09-24) -- has no such guard. The section-11 claim is stale/false for this file specifically: the repo's own convention was not mechanically enforced on new workflows, so it silently lapsed for the one file added after the claim was written.
population: 72 in-scope workflow files (.github/workflows/ files 1-74 per `ls .github/workflows` order, minus claude-pr-automerge.yml and pr-opener.yml which were out of CA-A13's scope). Of these, 28 are `on: issues:`-triggered and reference a secrets.* value other than GITHUB_TOKEN; 1 of 28 (3.6%) lacks the actor-guard.
blast_radius: If the repository's 'limit interactions to collaborators' interaction-limit setting (the sole remaining control, per the 2026-06-28 audit's own framing -- 'contained today, no defense-in-depth') is ever lapsed, misconfigured, or bypassed (e.g. a future outside collaborator with triage access, a compromised token that can apply labels), any actor able to apply the `gpu-burst-train` label to an issue reaches a job holding RUNPOD_API_KEY, VAST_API_KEY, RUNPOD_SSH_KEY, a trainer-VM SSH key (VM_SSH_KEY), and a repo-scoped PAT (BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN) -- with no second, identity-based gate to catch it, exactly the class of exposure section 3.3 of the June audit called 'remote code execution on the money-adjacent VM' for other, now-guarded workflows.
detector: None exists today. Checked scripts/ci/: check_workflow_catalog.py (doc-completeness only), check_workflow_trigger_reachability.py, check_workflow_push_target.py, check_workflow_failure_swallow.py, check_guard_liveness.py -- none inspects `issues:`-triggered workflows for an actor-identity guard. Proposed detector: a new CI guard (e.g. check_workflow_actor_guard.py) that parses every `.github/workflows/*.yml` with `on: issues:` and a `secrets.<NAME>` reference outside `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and fails the PR if the job's `if:` lacks an `issue.user.login`/`repository_owner`/`github.actor` clause -- mirroring how check_dry_run_in_diff.py already catches the analogous 'off is guarded, on is not' asymmetry for account/strategy gates.
proposed_fix: Add the Shape-A guard from docs/security/intrusion-surface-audit-2026-06-28.md section 9 to gpu-burst-train.yml's job `if:`, AND-ed onto the existing label check: `(github.event.issue.user.login == github.repository_owner || github.event.issue.user.login == 'github-actions[bot]') && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'gpu-burst-train')`. This is monotonic (can only deny, never grant) and matches the pattern already used by every sibling workflow. Separately, land the check_workflow_actor_guard.py CI guard described above so the next new privileged issues-triggered workflow cannot repeat this gap silently.
disposition: filed to pipeline as PI-20260927-CAA13-0001 (queued, next_action=dispatch_lane, due_when=observation, check_every_days=14)
